title: Separably generated and separable field extensions (not necessarily algebraic)
statement: Let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. A *transcendence basis* of $K/k$ is a family $(x_i)_{i\in I}$ of elements of $K$ that is algebraically independent over $k$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree] and such that every element of $K$ is algebraic over the subfield $k(x_i;i\in I)$. An algebraic extension $K/F$ is *separable algebraic* if the minimal polynomial over $F$ of every element of $K$ is separable (coprime to its derivative). $K$ is *separably generated over $k$* if there is a transcendence basis $(x_i)_{i\in I}$ of $K/k$ such that $K/k(x_i;i\in I)$ is separable algebraic. $K$ is *separable over $k$* if for every subextension $k\subset K'\subset K$ with $K'$ finitely generated as a field over $k$, the extension $K'/k$ is separably generated.
